recap.text: Carl builds a backpack for Katia, and the System labels it Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear. He loads it with metal poles and tiny xistera balls, and Katia, following a drawing on a gym membership form, reforms into a slug with a shelf on her back. The backpack lands and turns the colour of her flesh, and she stands eleven feet tall around a ton and a quarter of metal.

Katia's missiles-cracked chainsaw prize lies rumbling, twenty-five feet long, and Carl tells her to ready her backpack so they can bulk her up to lift it. An earthquake cuts her off. Firas tells Carl the house went into her inventory, then popped out over their heads in Cuttlefish Point. A boss box gives her an adjustable backpack with retractable stilts.

Louis tosses a potion bandolier at Katia, and it equips itself the moment it lands on her. Carl asks what the move is. Louis pitches it: she uses the new backpack to add mass, a giant breastplate drops on her from the Twister, then an even bigger helmet, like the Voltron formation sequence, sort of. Britney points out that if an item misses, Katia is crushed. Louis calls it a work in progress.

beats.headline: Backpacks were a thing
beats.text: Notes in the cookbook's margins argue about backpacks. Rosetta found that unstable satchels hold their stability in an equipped backpack, Allister confirmed it, and Forkith, mourning a little sister, says they only slow it now: he found that out the hard way. What Carl takes away is that backpacks are a thing, and he has an idea. He shows Katia the result on a stand he built for it and says he saw backpack listed on the armorer workshop tab, which is true. The System labels it Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear. Carl does not care, as long as the word Backpack is in there.
beats.gist: Carl builds a stand for his backpack, and he doesn't mind the System's absurdly long name for it.

beats.headline: A shell on her back
beats.text: Carl loads it with metal poles and a pour of tiny xistera balls. He has made it open-topped with a slight lip, so that it lists what is in it as contents. Katia is sure she will only get the backpack's own mass. Following a drawing on a gym membership form, she reforms into a slug-like shape with a shelf on her back, the stand clatters away, and the backpack lands on her and disappears, turning the colour of her flesh. The dense mass forms a rounded, shell-like shape. It worked. She tumbles onto her back like an overturned turtle, then reshapes herself round more than a ton of extra metal, closer to a ton and a quarter, Carl says, and stands about eleven feet tall with a strength bonus.
beats.gist: Katia loads the backpack with poles and xistera balls, then reshapes herself around it, eleven feet tall.

beats.headline: Thirty seconds is too long
beats.text: Katia spends the next hour practising with different masses. Taking it off through her inventory is inelegant: unequip more than half her mass at once and her body resets, splotching onto the floor as a quivering blob for a couple of seconds before she is herself again. Putting it on means setting up the redesigned stand, pulling the backpack onto it, backing in, strapping up and turning slug, and then forming whatever she wants from the mass she keeps in it. It takes about thirty seconds, which is still too long. They are working on it.
beats.gist: Katia practises for an hour, but putting the backpack on still takes thirty seconds.

beats.headline: Wider, with rubber
beats.text: Hekla wants Katia stuck to the front of a train as its cowcatcher, and it was Katia's own idea, she tells Carl in chat; it is why the Daughters are here. While he was gone, she altered the backpack on his engineering table and made it wider. There is more metal in it now, so she can make herself even bigger, and she has added rubber to the mix: layered between the metal and her flesh, it absorbs the impacts. What she needs is help with the design for the front of the train. She has to be careful of the third rail.
beats.gist: Katia widens the backpack with more metal and layered rubber so she can grow bigger and absorb impacts.

beats.headline: Bulk up for the saw
beats.text: Carl's missiles have done their job, and the prize lies rumbling on the ground: a still-chugging chainsaw that has to be twenty-five feet long. He did not want to damage it. Get your backpack ready, he tells Katia: they are going to bulk her up so she can lift the thing and stick it into her inventory. She starts to say something about how he is always complaining about the way they portray him, and a mighty rumble fills the world before she can finish. An earthquake.
beats.gist: Katia's backpack is to bulk her up to lift the twenty-five-foot chainsaw, when an earthquake interrupts her.

beats.headline: The house in her inventory
beats.text: Firas, down from the balloon-hung house with water arcing out of it behind him, tells Carl what he missed. It was Louis's idea. With the house floating just off the ground, Katia did that weird thing she does when she puts the backpack on, and it worked: the whole house went into her inventory. That same night, after the recap episode, they patched it, and the whole contraption popped out of her inventory over their heads in a pub called Cuttlefish Point. It almost smooshed them all, and it pretty much blew up the tavern.
beats.gist: Katia's backpack swallows the house; a patch makes it pop out over them.

beats.headline: Out of a boss box
beats.text: Katia gasps as she opens her boss box and a backpack appears. It is pretty much the same backpack Carl designed for her mass storage, she tells him, but it is adjustable, so she can carry even more, and it will not break. It gives her a stability enhancement while she is wearing it, and it has retractable stilts that make loading a lot easier. She can add large amounts of mass much more quickly now. Carl wonders whether they made something new for her or it had already been invented. She shrugs.
beats.gist: Katia opens a boss box and finds an adjustable, unbreakable backpack with retractable stilts.

beats.headline: Voltron, sort of
beats.text: Louis tosses a potion bandolier at Katia, and it equips itself the moment it lands on her. Carl asks what, exactly, the move is. The pitch: she has that new backpack that lets her add a bunch of mass, so let her get really big without a breastplate, drop a giant one on her from the Twister so it equips, let her get bigger, then drop an even bigger helmet. Like the Voltron formation sequence. Sort of. Unless the item misses or does not hit right, Britney points out, and she is crushed. It's a work in progress, says Louis.
beats.gist: Louis's plan is to drop armor on Katia to enlarge her; Britney says a miss crushes her.
